highlights.title: Upload Dexcom sensor states to Nightscout
changes: Trio can post a Note to Nightscout when a Dexcom G6/G7 reading has no reliable glucose.
The Note text uses the device kit's own state name (for example “CGM: sensorFailed” or “CGM: questionMarks”).
Each persistent problem is noted once and stays quiet until a reliable reading or a new sensor session clears it.
A new Upload CGM Sensor States switch appears in Nightscout upload settings and onboarding; it defaults off and also需要s.
Failed note uploads are retried automatically on the next CGM reading.

highlights.title: Fix keyboard auto-scrolling in Treatments
changes: Focused input fields in the Treatments screen now scroll into view above the keyboard.
The treatments list no longer stays hidden behind the keyboard on affected devices.
Unrelated keyboard appearances no longer trigger unexpected scrolling in the Treatments view.
A rare hang when tapping a field for the first time while debugging has been reduced.

highlights.title: Store calibrations as manual fingerstick readings
changes: Calibration readings from sensors are now stored as manual fingerstick glucose entries.
These entries are flagged as manual so the app treats them as user-entered readings.
Sensor calibrations are saved separately and are not used as CGM sgv values for processing.
If a CGM value is absent, Nightscout uses the manual calibration value for the reading.

highlights.title: Avoid crashes when rendering Override presets
changes: Opening the Override Presets list no longer crashes if a preset's identifier is missing or duplicated.
Corrupted or invalid duration and percentage values no longer crash the screen; those labels are quietly omitted.
Presets with valid data render exactly the same as before.

includedPullRequests.title: Report Dexcom sensor states to Nightscout as notes
includedPullRequests.body:
When a G6 or G7 reading carries no reliable glucose, Trio uploads a Note treatment with the kit's own name for the sensor state, for example "CGM: sensorFailed", "CGM: questionMarks" or "CGM: .unknown(23)". Trio holds no state table, titles or localizations for this: the kit's hasReliableGlucose decides whether a reading is noted, and the kit's description names it.

A state is noted once and stays quiet while it persists. A reliable reading or a new sensor session clears the log, so a state that returns after recovery is noted again. A failed upload is retried on the next reading. The notes are controlled by a new Upload CGM Sensor States switch under Services, Nightscout, Upload, and in the onboarding upload step; it defaults to off in settings and requires Allow Uploading to Nightscout. Lifecycle states without glucose (warmup, stopped, session ended, G6 initial calibration) are noted too, roughly two to four notes per sensor session.

Scope is Dexcom G6 and G7, since the state lives on the kit-specific latestReading. Libre 3, AccuChek and Eversense issue LoopKit alerts and can follow by mirroring those to notes in PluginSource.issueAlert.

Tests cover the reliability and naming rule, the dedupe log, and G7 transmitter messages fed through the real G7CGMManager. The upload path was exercised end to end against a Nightscout instance with a scripted state sequence.

includedPullRequests.title: Update TreatmentsRootView.swift to fix auto-scrolling and some (related) bugs
includedPullRequests.body:
Fixes issue #1115. Replaces PR #1365 which I accidentally screwed up when attempting to process the feedback.

**Issue summary:** 
The treatments menu would, when tapping the bolus screen, not scroll up properly on some devices. It would stay behind the keyboard.

**This PR:**
**1.)** fixes the problem and scrolls the focused field up properly. The first attempt (see aforementioned PR) relied on a hard-coded delay, about which feedback was given that it shouldn't be done that way. Therefore, this version is event driven/notification driven and tracks states. 

**2.)** Both in the previous version as this one: after the initial changes, the swift compiler would crash on a too large body (causing type-checker limit violation). To accommodate for this, the Reduced Bolus/Super Bolus toggles + Recommendation button + Bolus field + External Insulin toggle were extracted into their own "_ViewBuilder private var bolusSection: some View_", called from a single line in place of the original inline block. No logic should've been altered.

**3.)** Fixed a naming collision that occurred.

**4.)** Fixes a staleness bug in the queued-scroll state. "_pendingScrollTarget_" could be left set if focus cleared before the keyboard ever showed, and - since "_keyboardWillShowNotification_" fires app-wide, not scoped to this view - a later, unrelated keyboard appearance could act on that stale value and trigger an unexpected scroll.

This was fixed two ways: "_pendingScrollTarget_" is now cleared whenever focus becomes nil, and "_handleKeyboardWillShow_" re-validates that the queued target still matches the currently focused field before acting on it. Also cleared defensively on "_keyboardWillHide_" as a second safety net.

**5.)** Somehow, perhaps due to some re-arranging, it also fixes the problem that would cause the entire app to hang for +/- 10 seconds when a field was tapped for the first time whilst the app was running with the debugger attached. That wasn't the goal, but won't complain. (Not that it was a major issue... merely annoying when running XCode debugger.)

All of the above lives entirely within this file, confined to the scroll-related code. None of it should touch the bolus dosing logic or the Reduced Bolus/Super Bolus toggles' behavior or anything like that.

**Full-disclosure:**
The code has been generated and verified with the help of Claude and ChatGPT. Initial testing performed in production on iOS 26 on dev d1a66f4 (the previous version was tested on other dev versions obviously) by myself over the course of the last couple of weeks. Everything appears to be working as intended, no errors triggered and all fields behave as intended.

includedPullRequests.title: fix: store calibrations as manual fingersticks
includedPullRequests.body:
Currently, Eversense and AccuChek do not emit the calibrations to the app. I'm planning on changing this, but Trio records the manual readings as CGM readings.

This PR changes that by looking at the `wasUserEntered` property of [NewGlucoseSample](https://github.com/LoopKit/LoopKit/blob/dev/LoopKit/GlucoseKit/NewGlucoseSample.swift#L28). If this value is true, it will mark that reading as a manual glucose (adding the nice red waterdrop icon to the Trio main chart)

includedPullRequests.title: Fix two crash risks in Override preset row rendering
includedPullRequests.body:
Two related crashes are possible when the Override Presets list in Adjustments renders:

1. `ForEach(state.overridePresets)` relied on `OverrideStored`'s own `id` field for row identity, which is optional and can be nil (or, in principle, shared) on presets saved by an older build. SwiftUI hard-crashes when a ForEach sees a duplicate or nil id. Fixed by identifying rows with Core Data's own `objectID` instead, which is always present and always unique.

2. The row's duration and percentage labels used `Int(_: Decimal)` / `Int(_: Double)` directly, which traps (crashes) rather than failing gracefully if the stored value is NaN or out of Int's range. A preset with a corrupted duration or percentage would crash this screen on every open. Fixed by routing through Double's `isFinite`/range checks first, falling back to omitting that label instead of trapping.

Both are defensive fixes for corrupted/unusual saved data rather than changes to normal behavior -- presets with valid data render identically to before.
